done.why: I got the egg into the trophy case, opened and holding its golden canary. I also put in the chalice and the brass bauble. My goal was done. There was clearly much more underground (the dam, the river, places I never reached). But after a death, a maze and a long thief hunt, it felt like a natural place to stop.

about: An old white house in a forest sits over a big underground world. The egg is the heart of it. I could pick it up within minutes, but its clasp 'would take a professional's fingers to undo', so in practice it belongs to the thief. You let him rob you, follow him to his hideaway, beat him, and get the egg back opened. Then the clockwork canary inside sings for the songbird that brought the egg in the first place. It's about crooked help you never asked for, and a house waiting to be filled.

ending.what: The jewel-encrusted egg, opened by the thief and holding a golden clockwork canary, went into the trophy case with the chalice and the brass bauble. Score 92 of 350, Novice Adventurer.

moments.note: The nest description, a songbird 'with better taste in treasure than in architecture', made me grin.
The egg's clasp needs 'deft fingers, and not, one suspects, entirely honest ones'. A clear hint that only the thief can open it.
The trap door crashed shut and someone barred it behind me.
I typed a run of commands assuming a map I half-remembered. East led to a Round Room, not the dam, so about ten turns were wasted on things that weren't there.
The thief slipped through mid-'take all' and took the egg from me.
The southwest cave-in has rubble sorted into neat heaps, 'smallest nearest', with grit still trickling. Someone tidy has been down here.
I couldn't take the guidebook because my load was too heavy, 'the sword not least of it'. Juggling my load got fiddly.
I pushed a button and the thief stabbed me while I was standing next to him. My own fault for typing blind.
After I opened the sluice gates, the Loud Room became impassable and threw me out. My own actions changed the map.
The thief cut my throat in the Treasure Room. I died.
The death text was kind and specific: plain things strewn around the fields, 'somebody tidy has put the lamp back in the living room'. It was true, and recovering was easy.
The living room now shows a cyclops-shaped hole in the nailed door, which gave me a shortcut to the thief.
The thief died and the egg reappeared. Its clasp was 'undone ... as though it had been waiting for him'.
Winding the canary in the clearing and at Canyon View did nothing special. It only worked at the forest path by the tree.
The songbird came and dropped a brass bauble on my head. A lovely payoff.

wished: I wished I could carry more. The weight limit pushed me to drop things at the dam, and I never went back for them.
I wished the opened egg had led me somewhere besides the forest path. I tried winding the canary in three places before it worked.
I wished I could have explored the rest. The river, the dam's bubble, the coins in the maze and the stiletto were all left behind.
I wished there were a way to open the egg myself, or at least to try. The clasp text shut that down kindly but firmly.

lines.line: wedged into the fork of a branch by a songbird with better taste in treasure than in architecture.
lines.why: It set the tone: wry and affectionate.

lines.line: The clasp is jeweller's work, and would take a professional's fingers to undo without harm: deft fingers, and not, one suspects, entirely honest ones.
lines.why: The whole egg puzzle is in that one line.

lines.line: Somebody has sorted the near end of the rubble into neat heaps by size, smallest nearest.
lines.why: A small, strange human detail in a dead end. It felt like a clue about a person.

lines.line: anything of value has rolled into some dark corner in or under it, and somebody tidy has put the lamp back in the living room.
lines.why: A gentle, specific death penalty that told me exactly where to look.

lines.line: it stands open without a scratch on it, as though it had been waiting for him.
lines.why: It made the thief's role in the story feel almost tender.

lines.line: It has the patient air of something that expects to be filled.
lines.why: The trophy case as a character. It made filling it feel meaningful.

fun.why: The arc of being robbed, chasing the thief, dying, coming back, winning and then the canary payoff was satisfying. It was marred only by turns I wasted myself.

engagement.why: The thief kept me on edge, and each recovery after a setback pulled me forward.

difficulty.why: The egg hint was fair, and the cyclops, the maze and the thief fight were challenging but doable. Dying once to the thief felt earned. The canary location took some trial.

interestingness.why: Familiar shapes turned odd: a Round Room with tidily sorted rubble, a Loud Room that turns lethal after the dam, and a death that redistributes your belongings around the house.

prose.why: The new descriptions are witty and precise: the nest, the egg's clasp, the river 'in a hurry', the trophy case's patience.
